chapters.title: Zephaniah 1
body: Zephaniah opens about as severely as any prophetic book does — sweeping judgment named against idolatry and, pointedly, against those who've grown so complacent they say in their hearts, "the LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil." That particular complacency, not open rebellion, is named as its own kind of danger: assuming God is simply indifferent.

It's worth asking honestly whether some version of that quiet assumption has crept into your own faith — not denying God exists, just assuming he's not really paying attention either way. This chapter names that as worth taking seriously, precisely because it's so easy to drift into without ever deciding to.

chapters.title: Zephaniah 2
body: Judgment widens outward here to surrounding nations — Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia, Assyria — each named for specific pride and cruelty, especially toward Judah. The chapter's sharpest line lands on a "rejoicing city" that said, "I am, and there is none beside me," now reduced to a wasteland animals wander through. Self-sufficiency, stated that confidently, doesn't age well in Scripture.

Few of us would ever actually say "there is none beside me" out loud, but the posture it names — functioning as though we don't ultimately answer to anyone — can creep in quietly. This chapter doesn't need you to be a nation to take its warning personally.

chapters.title: Zephaniah 3
body: After naming Jerusalem's corrupt leaders, prophets, and priests directly, the chapter does something this series has seen before and still shouldn't lose its wonder: it turns, abruptly, into one of the tenderest pictures of God anywhere in Scripture — "he will rejoice over thee with joy... he will joy over thee with singing." Not grudging tolerance. Singing.

If you've only ever pictured God's attention toward you as evaluation — watching to catch what's wrong — this verse pictures something else entirely: delight, sung out loud, over someone genuinely loved. Whatever you believe you'd have to clean up first to be sung over like that, this chapter doesn't wait for it.
